newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end up on optimism after Japanese visit.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end up on optimism after Japanese visit.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up on Wednesday as investors perceived support for the economy from Japan after the visit to Peru of prime minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, brokers said.
The upbeat mood is expected to continue on Thursday, they added.

On Tuesday, Hashimoto signed loan agreements to Peru worth around $615 million for environmental, hydroelectric and road projects. He also said he would support the country's efforts to join the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation group (APEC).
On Wednesday, the General Index, rose 0.78 percent to 1,427.1 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index rose 1.16 percent to 1,949.0 points, according to preliminary stock figures.

"It was a heavy buying session -- particularly in Telefonica (del Peru," said Hugo Elcorobarrutia of local brokerage MGS. Accounting for 30 percent of the day's trade, benchmark Telefonica closed up 2.47 percent at 5.81 soles on volume of 1.83 million shares. Among other leaders, telecom Tele 2000 saw its price rise 1.19 percent to 4.25 soles, but its volume was low at 57,000 shares.
Luz del Sur rose 2.02 percent to 3.54 soles on volume of 3.0 million soles and chocolate producer D'Onofrio continued its bull run closing up 2.91 percent at 1.06 soles on volume of 723,000 shares.
Volume was 35.8 million soles ($14.5 million), where 46 stocks rose, 12 fell and 43 were stable.
